note: The check suite runs ONLY checks registered here (founding spec §4).
Registration requires an admission record: the named defect the check
caught or the contract it uniquely carries, the licensing issue, and a
removal signal declared at birth. An unregistered check file is dead
code; one meta check asserts the registry and the checks/ tree agree.
Every removal signal names its observing instrument (kogaki#113):
removal_instrument is `act: <the act that already happens and owes the
removal row>`, `none: <why no act in this repository can observe it>`,
or `probe: <tree-local shell predicate>` (exit 0 = the signal's
condition now holds; exit 1 = not yet; anything else = the probe could
not establish). Probes are evaluated by check-registry-conformance.sh,
which renders candidates report-only — removal stays a judgment.
Every admission record carries RE-EXECUTABLE EFFICACY EVIDENCE
(kogaki#243). The named defect above is a claim about what this check
CATCHES, and registration used to take it on the author's word —
constrain-generation applied to check EXISTENCE, never to check
EFFICACY. `efficacy` names the counterfactual instead: the case that
CONSTRUCTS the named defect and asserts the check REFUSES it.
`case: <path>::<verbatim label>` — the payload is the path, `::`,
and the label, WITH NOTHING APPENDED; human prose goes in the
sibling `efficacy_note`, on the convention `runtime_ms_note` sets.
`none: <why no counterfactual exists in this tree>` — the honest
state, and it is a MEASUREMENT rather than a deferral marker.
check-registry-conformance.sh refuses a `case:` unless <path> exists
and contains <label> literally and EXACTLY ONCE. What that buys,
claimed precisely because overstating it would be the very defect
kogaki#243 names: editing or deleting the cited text breaks the entry
that cites it, and a label too generic to identify one case is
refused as non-unique. What it does NOT decide: that the cited text
is a COMPLETE case label rather than part of one, or that it occurs
in code rather than in a comment. Both are judgments about meaning,
and a language-aware parser for them would be a lint over judgment.
Shape and resolution are gated; whether the counterfactual is a GOOD
one is judgment and is never gated — the split `probe:` runs under.

admission.contract: the consult-first discipline's reading act: reports the branch's consulted: receipt count and distinct pins, rendering zero explicitly — an obligation generates no event to hook, so observability is the whole remedy. Fails only on a malformed receipt, never on the count. Fenced-block quotations are MENTIONS of the grammar, not receipts, and are excluded from the counted set (kogaki#41, the PR #40 false positive). Parses the v2 continuation block (kogaki#28, story 1.10) — request_id, outcome, one query line per framing, indented under line one, all OPTIONAL so every v1 receipt in git history stays valid — and widens malformed to SIX field defects, all conformance rather than counting: an outcome outside the hub's ratified triple (a bare `miss` collapses the two causes the 2026-08-02 correction separated), a re-framed outcome recording fewer than every framing's query, an `uncovered-after-N` whose N disagrees with the number of query lines recorded (shape validation alone let a receipt claim seven framings while recording two), an N below the two-framing floor (a miss is not recordable as uncovered until re-asked along another axis; the floor is stated as its own clause because it is currently also implied by the query rule, and an implied invariant is one a refactor drops unnoticed), and a PARTIAL v2 receipt — continuations stay optional so a v1 receipt is valid, but once ANY continuation is present the receipt owes all three fields SPEC §4 requires (PR #43 review). The embedded fixture pass is the discrimination evidence, run every invocation, and asserts the PARSED FIELDS rather than only counts — a count-only assertion cannot observe whether the continuation fields were read at all, which measured 2 of 8 v2 cases discriminating before the assertion was widened and 6 of 8 after. States what it does NOT verify: the query-count rule is satisfied by two rephrasings of one question, and axis-variation is a judgment no count can observe — the check asserts the framings were RECORDED and routes whether they differed to the review lane, with a receipt found carrying two rephrasings as the observation that would earn a real detector. Empty values are handled by ONE rule applied in the parse: continuation PRESENCE is recorded as a fact about the text rather than inferred from value truthiness, and an empty value is absent for every field alike — before which empty query lines counted as recorded framings, so `uncovered-after-3-framings` with three blank queries satisfied N == len() (PR #43 re-review), and a `query:` line holding a SERIALIZED TOOL ARGUMENT rather than a question (kogaki#160 finding 4): the field is defined at the consultation map's Miss-postmortem field as the question verbatim, the grammar accepted any non-empty value, and `query: {"tag":"lessons/claude-code-ops"}` shipped on master passing every clause above — because the transport DERIVED the line, reading it off policy_lookup's own `question` argument and falling back to the raw --args JSON for every other tool, so a gloss_index consult had no field in which to record its question. gateway-query.mjs now requires `--question` per `--args` and refuses without it, making the emission unproducible on the tool path; this clause is the floor under condition 2's marked-exception path, and is the narrowest rule that discriminates — a value that is a JSON object/array end to end is a tool argument, while a question CONTAINING braces or quotes passes, with fixtures in both directions. Backward compatible by the scan window: this check reads merge-base..HEAD plus the PR body, never a file on the default branch and never the whole history, so receipts already merged lie outside every future scan and no branch fails on work it did not author. THE SECOND AXIS (kogaki#268): a `disposition:` continuation key carrying the GATE half — what the gate did with the consultation — on its own field rather than in `outcome:`, which is where the digest's vocabulary claim assumed it lived and where this check's own ratified-triple clause refuses it. Three vocabularies in this seam are called `outcome` and two of them are mutually exclusive in one slot, so the resolution is one field per axis, each owned by whoever must agree on it: the values are ADOPTED verbatim from the ratified closed two-value set (`auto-resolved-FYI | escalated`, spec-policy-fork-consultation §"Amended 2026-07-21 (triage, #519)", "no consumer-local extension") because a field read by both sides of the boundary is the boundary's and the boundary's owner is the hub (`topics/knowledge-architecture.md:31@dec0d568`), while the field's SHAPE is this repository's. The key is OPTIONAL and is deliberately NOT added to presence-implies-completeness' owed set: most consults here are not fork gates, and requiring the field would force a value on them. Recognising the key in the checker is a REQUIREMENT rather than a convenience — the continuation scan stops at the first unrecognised indented key, so a receipt carrying `disposition:` above its query lines parsed on the pre-#268 scanner as a field-less v1 line with every later field silently dropped, and 10 of the 12 new fixtures fail that scanner spliced against this fixture table. What it does NOT make substantiable, stated rather than implied: `consult-miss` and `degraded` stay uncountable from receipts under this or any schema — an unconsulted fork emits no receipt and a degraded consult emits none by design — so both are refused as values with that reason named, and the report line counts the two dispositions and says what nothing here can count WIDENED (kogaki#336): the grammar gains a THIRD continuation key, `axis:`, and it is the first that binds PER QUERY — upward to the nearest preceding `query:`, first declaration wins, an axis before any query orphaned and reported. The check validates SHAPE ONLY — position and a non-empty token — because the `subject | conduct` value set is the hub's to ratify under the boundary-field rule (product-lab@4cc496b topics/knowledge-architecture.md:50), so any value passes and unknown ones are reported and denied nowhere; the report NAMES the distinct axes rather than only counting them, which is what makes an unratified set observable while it is unratified. Eight per-query binding cases exercise both directions, plus an explicit never-gates assertion that an unknown axis is not reported malformed — the assertion standing between shape-only and this repository silently minting boundary values it does not own. Runtime re-measured 80 -> 95 ms (three local runs) for the widening rather than for an admission, because the binding quantity is cost per ship-cycle rather than member count.

admission.contract: the client kit's install guarantees, fired rather than merely written: fresh-install layout, idempotency, the one-line degrade at exit 11, the pinless-body deny, harness-loadable skill frontmatter, the entry-2 boundary (no kit tool reads gateway state), and the absence of any colocation default. Also the transport's RECEIPT MODE (kogaki#66, story 1.20), where the emitter replaces hand transcription: the refusal to assign the `outcome` token — `deferred-slot: consult-outcome-token-assignment` is FILLED (owner decision 2026-08-06, kogaki#66 — the OPERATOR supplies the token), so a default would reinstate the guess the fill declined and the refusal must still name the slot rather than read as a syntax error; that a degraded run emits NO receipt block, because a receipt for a consult that did not happen is the fabrication the clause exists to prevent; that receipt mode is opt-in, so the pre-1.20 invocation is byte-for-byte unchanged; that the marked-exception key is the fixed UNINDENTED `consult-receipt:` token, which is correctness rather than style because check-consult-receipts.sh recognises only request_id/outcome/query as continuation keys and an unrecognised indented key above them ends the continuation scan, leaving a field-less v1 line that silently passes; and the emitter's own 13-case composition fixture pass, which asserts line one is COPIED from the served response rather than re-derived, one query line per framing actually run, pins merged under one commit, the token carried untouched, and five refusals where the wire did not carry what a receipt asserts. Also the consult ENTRY POINT (kogaki#94, story 1.21), whose properties are all properties of the INVOCATION rather than of the wire and so are decidable without a reachable gateway: that there is exactly ONE receipt composer and the entry point is not a second one, routing through the transport instead; that a verdict-shaped input is corrected AT THE POINT OF USE and never forwarded (exit 3), and that the correction is an affordance — `--restate` re-submits the corrected claim in the same act and the run then reaches the wire, which is the only observable distinguishing an affordance from a nicer denial; that `--outcome` is required at the entry point as on the transport, with the refusal naming the OPERATOR, because the entry point is the surface a session touches; that the two-framings floor is carried at the call in BOTH directions (refused with what the re-framing owes, and proceeding once the second framing is supplied), since a floor that refused everything would pass a one-directional test; that the framing COUNT is emitted as the transport fact it is and a token contradicting it is refused rather than repaired, repair being the tool assigning the token by the back door; that the re-framing bound is ONE, never a search loop; and that the exit-11 degraded path is STATED with its example receipt marker UNINDENTED above line one, asserted on the emitted text because a wrong example is a wrong receipt in every PR that follows it. What no case on either surface covers is a LIVE consult, which the test states rather than leaves to look covered. Registered because a test nothing invokes is the orphan-guard shape kogaki#6 was filed to end Also the ISSUE-CHECKPOINT CONTENT-LIVENESS half (kogaki#188), where the guarantee is that a pass-claim matches what was actually compared: that the THIRD entry point `--emit-pin-quotes` owes the same one-line exit-11 degrade as the other two, because it is the WRITER for the stored quote hash and a writer that emits a short list on an unreachable seam reads as a complete one; and the tool's own content-liveness fixture pass, which is pure and gateway-free and asserts the whitespace-normalized hash (a reflowed served line is the same quote, while a case flip is not), use-vs-mention on BOTH the pin-quote and consulted grammars, a DECLARED served-address map that returns cannot-tell rather than guessing an address, the live topics/articles.md:79 drift blocked AND located at :80 as the regression pin (the dangerous form is the pin that still RESOLVES, so a resolution check cannot catch it), three results rather than two with `verified` reachable only through a fetch that returned records in scope, and an output that never implies liveness it did not check. Widened at this admission act rather than left to be inferred from the case list Also the SHAPE READ and the EMISSION DUTY (kogaki#325/#326, stories 1.48/1.49), the kit's two default-on consumer clauses, whose install-time properties are decidable without a reachable gateway and are therefore asserted here: that the shape read is gitignored EXACTLY ONCE across two installs and that the emission directory is NOT gitignored — the two assertions are deliberately INVERSE, because the artifacts answer the same axis oppositely on source sensitivity rather than on file kind, and asserting only one would leave a later change free to 'make them consistent' and destroy the distinction the spec exists to record, with the failure silent and, on a public repository, irreversible once pushed; that the managed CLAUDE.md block carries BOTH clauses, since specs/spec-client-kit/SPEC.md §2 refuses skill-as-sole-carrier and a clause reaching only the sittings that invoke a skill is the failure the default carrier exists to prevent; that the shape read degrades in ONE line at exit 11 like every other kit tool, which the install itself depends on because a hard failure there would break the ratified degraded-install-is-a-valid-install promise for every consumer; that the emission writer produces the five fixed fields at a dated, slugged path, prints that path as an in-session receipt, and refuses an undeclared grain, the set being closed like every other declaration here; that the emitted text ITSELF states it is a candidate and not a promotion, asserted on the artifact rather than trusted to the prose above it, because §4.2's emission-is-not-promotion boundary is this writer's entire standing; that the plain-register note REPORTS without refusing and the write still exits 0, a channel that rejects your words being a channel you stop using; and both tools' own gateway-free fixture passes. What no case here covers is a LIVE digest composition, which needs a reachable seam and is stated rather than left to look covered. Also the OWNER REGISTER's install-time half (kogaki#320, story 1.50): that the owner-render fixture pass runs; that the RELAY RULE in the installed skill points at the kit's emission and assigns the Conclusion to the agent — asserted against the INSTALLED copy, which is what caught this story editing the installed file while leaving the kit SOURCE untouched, the kogaki#285 divergence reproduced live and fixed in the same act; and that a DEGRADED consult emits NEITHER register, because a rendering of an answer that was never served is the same fabrication the no-receipt-on-degrade rule already forbids. Separability (AC2) is asserted where transportArgv lives rather than here — the entry point is not import-safe, so a node -e import cannot reach the function; this member invokes that pass and the arrangement is named in the test so the coverage stays findable. Also the DELTA STEP (kogaki#334, story 1.51), which is the shape read's §3.4 act and the first case here that needs a STUB GATEWAY: the earlier shape-read cases establish properties of a RENDERING, decidable from a degrade and a pure fixture pass, whereas a delta is a property of a COMPARISON against a live regeneration — a vendored pin differing from a served one — and no state of an unreachable gateway produces that, so the wire is doubled rather than the content asserted. Four properties, all on emitted text: that a stale vendored pin REPORTS AND EXITS 0, because §3.5's enhancer-never-dependency property makes a pre-step that gates a sitting the defect rather than the feature; that no vendored digest AT ALL is its own third state and also exits 0, an absent digest and an unchanged one being the same quiet and different facts; that the output is PIN-FREE — no `consulted:`, no `request_id:`, no `@<sha>` — because §8 puts pins on the machine-facing side and a delta shown before a sitting is the one shape-read output an owner reads directly, asserted on live text as well as in the fixture pass since the fixture composes its own inputs while this carries a real pin through the whole composer; and that `--delta` owes the same one-line exit-11 degrade every other kit tool owes. Also the PER-TERM DENOMINATOR (§3.1's clause as amended by kogaki#334), which is the element-level three-state rendering PR #335 landed, surviving one grain down: `if (e.soft) continue;` made a term whose own `glossary_entry` read could not be parsed indistinguishable from one carrying no state line, so the section rendered its survivors as the whole in-scope set. The stub serves an unparseable body for one in-scope term and the case asserts that term is COUNTED AND NAMED in the digest — an end-to-end assertion the gateway-free fixtures cannot make, and the reason this widening is not simply more fixture cases. AND, added kogaki#285, the BYTE-EQUALITY of the kit source `policy/kit/skills/consult-first.md` with THIS repository's installed copy `.claude/skills/consult-first/SKILL.md` — asserted over the real tree rather than the temp install, because `install.sh` copies source over copy and a divergence is a pending SILENT DELETION of whichever side is not the source rather than a conflict. The kit's own test structurally cannot carry this: it installs into `mktemp -d` and asserts over a result that is a `cp` of the source by construction, so it passes identically while the committed copy has drifted.

The detection half behind terrain/terrain.mjs's generation-time refusal (validateSurvey applies the same schema-carried rules before writing); the fixture pass is the evidence both halves discriminate. Carries composition FACTS only and says so in its own output; whether the grouping axis serves the owner and whether a ratified narrowing was worth taking are judgment and route to kogaki#13 PLUS the composition contracts the member has since grown to carry, named here because an admission record whose `contract` does not describe what the member covers is not recording what is carried (kogaki#145): §6.1/§6.2's co-tag screen — GroupClaim served first, member Lesson IDs for every group without --group, SubGroups judged at the screen with their leaf verdict and disclosures and a required judge pin, and no member-count threshold in the split logic; §7's claim lifecycle — the re-offer's three origin branches (record, screen-composed, absent) and whether an origin's member set was recorded or DERIVED; §9's screen-1 tag-row allowlist — the tag name and its Lesson count and nothing else, composed through the single `tagRow` constructor; and §12's Full Report — the identity triple (substrate pin, co-tag query, judge pin) with `none` typed, its four idempotence cases counted over real artifacts, and the eager --all-groups fan-out with its pre-write judge-pin refusal; and §8's `subdivide` COMMAND — the command path run end to end rather than only its exported composers, its record written past the instruments loop, the third instrument reading the judge's own verdict rather than a literal, and the PLACEMENT-COMPOSED `(fits no composed SubGroup)` SubGroup — EXPLICIT and named, which is the property the cover contract refuses to give up — carrying all three instruments (kogaki#165: from story 1.31 until that fix `subdivide` raised ReferenceError on every invocation, and no registered check invoked the command, so every exercised path masked a dead command); and §9's BOUNDED COMPOSITION INPUT — `compose-input`'s one tag-scoped shard pair per run with the journey half fetched only where a member carries one, its groups carrying IDS ONLY so a per-group material copy is unwritable, and the read count held CONSTANT across a record whose placements were multiplied over the same candidates, observed at the command by a stub gateway counting the reads it served rather than read off the accounting the run printed about itself (kogaki#163: a self-reported count is the system's own explanation of what it did, which is not evidence of it). The artifact-counting and seam-reading blocks report CANNOT-DETERMINE where the served seam is absent rather than passing or failing. PLUS §13.4's THREE RENDERING PROPERTIES over the provenance-neighborhood screen (kogaki#303, story 1.45): every rendered suggestion NAMES the substrate that reached it, with a substrate-less row rendering an explicit undisclosed marker rather than an empty `reached by:`; denominators stated PER FAMILY and never pooled, read from the batch records' own family-keyed `members` rather than re-derived from the served element set, with a family carrying no `members` list rendering an explicit no-denominator note rather than `of 0`; and an unresolved reference NAMED WITH ITS VALUE while the 12 legacy `q_a/N/answer.md` batches must NOT be marked, which is what stops the property passing vacuously by marking everything. Asserted over the COMPOSED LINES via the exported `neighborhoodScreen`, not over the enumerator: an enumerator returning a disclosed structure that the screen prints bare satisfies story 1.44's block and ships the defect.

admission.contract: the boundary-receipt binding at the merge layer (specs/SPEC.md §4, kogaki#25): a consultation-map boundary whose trigger terms MATCH the branch, with ZERO receipts present, FAILS — which is what converts the map from advice an agent may remember into a carrier that binds on every PR. A PRESENCE CHECK OVER TWO DECLARED ENUMERATIONS (the map's entries, the branch's receipts), both named in the output because a coverage claim is a fraction OF an enumeration. It NEVER BRANCHES ON THE OUTCOME TOKEN and structurally cannot: it reads line one only, so `discriminating`, `covered-after-reframing` and `uncovered-after-N-framings` satisfy it alike — the obligation is TO ASK and never TO HAVE FOUND (as corrected for kogaki#32), and a check that passed on some outcomes and failed on others would be judging whether the consultation SUCCEEDED, which is the review lane's property. LINE ONE ONLY also keeps it independent of the v2 continuation block (kogaki#28, story 1.10), whose validation stays with check-consult-receipts.sh — that check's report-never-gate contract is not absorbed, redefined or deleted, because this one gates a DIFFERENT property. It BINDS PRESENCE, NOT ORDER: a receipt written after the code it should have preceded satisfies it exactly as one written before, nothing in this repository observes that ordering, and the gap is stated rather than assumed covered (observed live on the story-1.10 branch). THE ATTRIBUTION HALF IS CARRIER-LESS AND MARKED: line one names a pin, never a boundary, so one receipt satisfies every matched boundary and a PR touching two while consulting one passes — carrier-less by omission is the defect, carrier-less with a reopen trigger is admissible (topics/knowledge-architecture.md:52@ed47fbd). FALSE POSITIVES ARE ACCEPTED AND DISCHARGED rather than narrowed away: an incidental term match is answered by the same act a real one asks for, so a spurious match costs one consultation rather than a false verdict — the map's ratified accretion polarity preserved at gate severity (owner decision at implementation; narrowing to diff paths alone was considered and declined as a silent shrink of what the map binds). THE SOURCE SET IS DECLARED and so is what it could not read — diff paths, changed text (commit messages, PR body), and the linked issue body, with an unavailable source NAMED rather than passed over, since an instrument that reports absence without establishing it is the defect the review lane refuses one layer up (carried by the engine since kogaki#630 retired check-review-report.sh with the stack); an unreadable or unparseable map is COULD NOT ESTABLISH and fails, in its own wording, because a fallback worded as a finding accuses. The embedded fixture pass runs every invocation and needs no network, firing BOTH discriminating cases — matched+receipt passes, matched+none fails — plus source coverage, outcome-invariance, line-one-only, use-vs-mention, and the word-bound case that keeps short terms from matching inside longer words. AND THE PATH SET IS THE BRANCH'S OWN, COMPUTED AT THE FORK POINT (kogaki#264): CI supplies `github.event.pull_request.base.sha` — the base branch's TIP at event time — and `git diff A..B` is a tree diff rather than a range, so every file that landed on master after this branch forked entered the path set and matched a boundary, at DENY severity, naming a file the branch never touched; the neighbouring `git log` and `git rev-list` read the same string as a genuine range, so the report printed a truthful commit count beside a path set of a different span. Paths, commits and count now all read the FORK POINT's span, and the output NAMES the fork point and says when the supplied base has advanced past it. The repair is sited in the check and not in the workflow because `base.sha` is a truthful name for a truthful value whose other consumers read it only through range operators, and because no fixture in this repository can watch a YAML expression. It does NOT reopen the kogaki#126 decline of narrowing to diff paths alone — that decline rests on path matches being the reliable signal, which this defect poisoned — and adds no judgment clause: matcher, sources and output vocabulary are untouched

admission.contract: the external-dependency registry (specs/SPEC.md:69-80, specs/spec-external-deps/SPEC.md; kogaki#55): the capabilities this repository NEEDS but cannot install, declared in deps/registry.json and read at run time rather than assumed. The specimen is the held run on PR #51, where three obstacles — the spawned reviewer's tool grants, the repository's allow_auto_merge, the merge deny's install state — were ONE defect, all assumed and none declared, so an unmet dependency presented as a stall or as a grant that was silently impossible to exercise. Reads specs/spec-external-deps/deps-schema.json's field lists rather than restating them, the same single-carrier arrangement check-gate-carrier.sh has against gate-schema.json. CONFORMANCE IS ITS SUBJECT AND THE WORLD IS A REPORT: it fails on a malformed or incomplete entry and never on an unmet dependency — the schema's own never_fails_on list, the same split this registry's consult-receipts entry already records ('Fails only on a malformed receipt, never on the count'), because whether a setting elsewhere is flipped changes without anyone touching the diff under review. EVERY ROW IS RENDERED, INCLUDING THE ZEROES: each decidable verification is EXECUTED and its result printed present or absent, each non-decidable entry's typed `none: <why>` is printed as its own row rather than omitted (a reason is evidence, an omission is not), and an empty registry's zero is printed through the same code path a fixture asserts, because a silent pass is indistinguishable from a check that did not run. A READ THAT DID NOT COMPLETE IS NOT AN ABSENCE: a command exiting non-zero is COULD-NOT-ESTABLISH on its own row and never 'absent', and every read runs under a hard timeout so a hanging network call cannot cost the pre-push loop unboundedly. The non-member fallback is carried rather than promised: deps/registry.json's observed_non_members list is rendered whether empty or not, and a recorded non-member stating no reason FAILS — admit-with-disclosure made checkable, which is the load-bearing half of an enumeration that can never be complete. States what it does NOT carry: nothing in this repository DETECTS that an act depended on an undeclared capability, so that list is hand-written and the observation half is carrier-less with a reopen trigger rather than carrier-less by omission; and whether a declared read answers the question its `answers` line claims, and whether an absence_signature is the signature the absence really leaves, are judgment and route to kogaki#13. The embedded fixture pass runs every invocation and needs no network: 12 entry-shape cases (conformant and malformed both fired), the four verification-read states including the two never-fails-on cases asserted by state rather than only by not-failing, duplicate ids, both directions of the non-member fallback, and the empty-registry rendering

admission.contract: the .claude tracking boundary (kogaki#618, consequence 3 of kogaki#615's owner ruling of 2026-08-22): every path in `git ls-files '.claude/*'` carries a `!<path>` re-include line in .gitignore, anchored whole so a directory re-include cannot stand in for a file's. The default-deny .gitignore block is the generator fix and removes the ordinary way a private harness path re-enters tracking; `git add -f` bypasses gitignore entirely, so this member is the enumerated layer beneath that constraint, catching the bypass (constrain-generation-not-post-hoc-detection: the enumerated list is a fast path beneath the construction constraint, never in place of it). The assertion is a SUBSET RELATION rather than a file list, so it holds for admissions nobody has made yet and needs no editing when one is argued. It cannot leak a private filename: both sides of the comparison are public by construction — a tracked path is in the tree and the allowlist is in .gitignore — and a path that is neither is never read. States what it does NOT verify: whether a re-include's public-need argument is TRUE, or whether the path still has the reader its comment names; both are judgment and stay with review, per authenticate-facts-mechanically-gate-judgments. An empty tracked set renders its explicit zero rather than passing silently.
admission.removal_signal: the boundary itself going away — the repository turning private, or tracking under .claude/ being re-ruled so that no path needs an argued admission. At that point the subset relation has no privacy property to protect and the member's premise is gone.
admission.removal_instrument: act: the PR that lands either change (a visibility flip, or a successor to kogaki#615's ruling) owes this check's removal row in the same act; until then the .gitignore allowlist is the only carrier of a path's public-need argument and this is the only thing asserting the argument exists
admission.efficacy: case: checks/check-claude-boundary.sh::FAIL: ${#violations[@]} tracked .claude path(s) carry no re-include in .gitignore.
admission.efficacy_note: MUTATION EVIDENCE (assert-by-breaking-once, run 2026-08-23 under kogaki#618, each mutation applied once and restored): `git add -f .claude/settings.json` — a path admitted through the exact bypass this member exists to catch — failed the check, which named settings.json and no other path; and deleting the `!.claude/skills/terrain/SKILL.md` re-include from .gitignore while the path stayed tracked failed it naming that path, which is the same relation broken from the allowlist side rather than the index side. The two mutations are the relation's two directions and are stated separately rather than as one row, because a check that caught only the add-side would pass an allowlist silently edited to drop an argument. The clean state renders `all 5 tracked path(s) carry a re-include`.
